judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY TWO Performance Objectives under the same Theme (Mensuration and Geometry) and Sub-Theme (Shapes). The first asks pupils to identify 2D shapes (square, rectangle, circle, triangle) under Topic 2 'Two dimensional shapes'; the second asks pupils to identify and count the edges of a cube and cuboid under Topic 1 'Three dimensional shapes'. They share substantive conceptual coherence as complementary shape-recognition/geometry objectives, but the high text overlap is dominated by shared boilerplate ('pupils should be able to identify a'), and the actual skills differ (recognizing 2D figures vs. analyzing edges of 3D solids). They sit at the same grade rank with no source-backed evidence that proficiency in one is required for or clearly precedes success in the other, so a developmental buildsTowards direction is not supported. relatesTo best captures the reinforcing conceptual link within the Shapes sub-theme.

judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Money' (Sub-Theme Primary Measures, Theme Mensuration and Geometry, Grade PRIMARY TWO, same rank). The first objective ('recognize all types of Nigerian coins and bank notes') establishes currency recognition, a foundational skill that supports the second objective ('change money up to ₦20 into small units and shop with money not greater than ₦20'), which requires identifying denominations to make change and transact. Proficiency in recognition therefore supports success in the applied money-handling objective, justifying a directional build from first to second even at equal grade rank. The shared 'money' LC token and page proximity are corroborating but not decisive; the pair-specific skill progression carries the judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives (same rank 0) under the same Theme (Number and Numeration) and Sub-Theme (Whole Number). The first arranges numbers 6-9 by magnitude (ordering); the second writes numbers 1-99 (numeral writing). These are distinct but complementary whole-number numeration skills that reinforce number sense, supporting relatesTo. There is no clear developmental dependency: ordering a small set by magnitude does not specifically build toward writing a larger range of numerals nor vice versa, and the shared-parent/token overlap is largely boilerplate ('numbers','the','should','be','able','to'), so buildsTowards is not warranted.

The first objective develops the core computational skill of dividing whole numbers up to 48 by 2-6 without remainder; the second requires carrying out correct division in everyday activities. Mastery of the concrete division procedure meaningfully supports success in applying division to everyday contexts, justifying a lower-to-higher developmental direction from computation to application (first_to_second). Shared 'division' LC tag and topic corroborate substantive coherence beyond mere hierarchy/wording overlap.
